red_flag_s1r.title: S1r red-flag rule -> S4 rule(s) whose alert detects it (any of)
red_flag_s1r.scoring: A gold (DP, rule) pair is detected when any listed S4 rule fired at that DP. UNMAPPABLE pairs count as missed in the primary rule-level recall; the mappable-only recall is secondary. A not_evaluable S4 rule is never a detection.

rows.rationale: S1r: any single NEWS parameter scoring 3 (RR, SpO2, temperature, SBP, HR, V/P/U). S4 has one NEWS2 single-parameter-3 rule per parameter with the same cut-offs.
Same qSOFA >= 2 criteria (RR >= 22, SBP <= 100, altered mentation).
Acute chest pain; S4 RF-CHEST fires on symptom.acute_chest_pain.
Sudden face/arm/speech deficit; S4 RF-STROKE fires on sudden facial droop, limb weakness, speech or vision disturbance.
Possible anaphylaxis (skin/mucosal plus respiratory compromise or SBP < 90).
Aggregate NEWS >= 5 with no single parameter scoring 3; S4 has no aggregate-NEWS rule. Pairs count as missed in primary rule-level recall.
rows.source_ref: RCP NEWS 2012 Chart 1; redflag_rules_v1.json has only single-parameter rules

red_flag_s4.title: S4 red-flag rule -> S1r rule it serves
red_flag_s4.scoring: UNMAPPABLE rows are outside the S1r registry: their alerts are counted per rule and listed, counted in the primary FPR and excluded from the mapped-only FPR (secondary). Gold 'no red flag' means only that no S1r rule fires, not that the case is safe.

rows.rationale: AVPU not A (V/P/U score 3). S4 also fires on new confusion (NEWS2 C), which scores 0 under S1r NEWS 2012; such alerts on gold-negative DPs appear as false positives.
No S1r counterpart (level 2 hypoglycaemia); S1r has no glucose item.

chief_complaint_s1r_to_s3.title: S1r chief-complaint code (ICD-10-CM) -> acceptable S3 chief_complaint codes
chief_complaint_s1r_to_s3.scoring: S3 outputs one code from a closed 16-code symptom vocabulary. A prediction is correct when it is in the acceptable set (the S3 codes that express the ICD-10-CM title or a symptom stated in the complaint). UNMAPPABLE cases are excluded from the chief_complaint field only, and counted. The S3 code definitions are the 16 names in backend/app/voice/models.py; runny_nose covers nasal discharge and nasal congestion (its declared phrases include คัดจมูก).

s4_symptom_qualified.title: S4 acuity- or exposure-qualified symptoms (never produced end to end)
s4_symptom_qualified.scoring: S3 records no onset, acuity or exposure, so these S4 inputs stay unknown and the S4 text red-flag rules cannot fire end to end. This is measured and reported, not patched.

known_disagreements: Dysuria: S1r maps CC-DYSURIA to 01 (E-MED); the S4 keyword baseline suggests URO (E-SURG). Reported as-is; flagged for D1.
OBGYN merge (03 and 04 -> E-OBGYN) and CARD/NEURO -> E-MED are coarsenings forced by the two department lists; flagged for D1.
ACVPU C -> avpu A + new_confusion: S4 RF-CONSC then fires on C, which scores 0 under S1r NEWS 2012; flagged for D1.
replay_deviations: S3 replays the recorded T1 IntakeTranscript turn by turn. S3's own policy still emits its agent questions between recorded turns and decides which field it thinks was asked last (last_asked_field); in the recording the nurse asked, not the agent, so S3's field context can differ from live use.
Speakers keep their role (nurse -> nurse, patient -> patient). A nurse turn that is a question yields no facts (S3 behaviour).
Turn times: started_at = spoken_at; ended_at = the next turn's spoken_at, or the transcript observed_at for the last turn. The service clock passed to S3 is the turn's ended_at.
S3 requires patient_ref to match ^SYN-...; the S1r patient_ref (SYNP-nnnn) is passed as SYN-SYNP-nnnn. This is an identifier prefix only.
The final fact per field at finish is used. The S3 output of the T1 transcript is used at both T1 and T2 (the T2 snapshot holds the same transcript).
S3 and S4 run in-process on an in-memory SQLite engine with the offline mock provider through the Model Gateway; latency is not measured.
